stem: In the gas phase (with solvation effects removed), arrange the following from STRONGEST to WEAKEST base toward a proton: an alkyl anion (R3C-), hydroxide (OH-), fluoride (F-), and the amide ion (NH2-).
opts: OH- > F- > NH2- > alkyl
F- > OH- > NH2- > alkyl
Alkyl > NH2- > OH- > F-
NH2- > alkyl > OH- > F-
All four are equally strong bases
why: All four are anions on second-row atoms, so the deciding factor is electronegativity. Across the period it rises (C < N < O < F), and the more electronegative the atom, the better it tolerates the negative charge and the weaker it is as a base. The carbanion is therefore the strongest base and fluoride the weakest: alkyl > NH2- > OH- > F-.
note: FIX: stem and choices named neutral NH3, which is a far weaker gas-phase base than OH- or F-, so the keyed order was wrong. Changed to the amide ion NH2- that the periodic-trend reasoning intends.
